Remove all the alternative hosts for citrus psyllid vector such as kie-apples around farm.
Space the plants about 10 -15 feet apart to reduce possible vector build up and infection.
Plant tissue culture cleaned propagating materials.
Select wind protected sites or plant wind breakers around the orchard to avoid wind blowing of the citrus psyllid vectors to the orchard.
Conserve the natural enemies in the enviroment such as lady beetle, parasitic wasp and other predators to suppress psyllid population by growing flowering plants such as lantana.
Monitoring: Inspect regularly for yellowing on single shoots or branch for first appearance of early symptoms.
Set up pheromone traps and monitor the citrus psyllid (vector) infestation in the orchard in between the rows of the orchard and take action when more than 5 psyllids are observed per trap.
Look out for small upright shoots with short internodes, stiff and partially folded leaves (Rabbit ears).
Look out for stunted plants with premature leaf drop, twig die back and decay of lateral shoots.
Take action when 1-2 plants are affected.
Direct Control: Uproot or prune infected plant and destroy by burning the infected debris.

Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB)
